results.content:
Among registered voters, Democrats led the generic congressional ballot 42 percent to 37 percent. Independents favored Democratic candidates by 12 points.

Reuters/Ipsos surveyed 4,505 U.S. adults nationwide online July 30-August 3. The poll had a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

## Competitive Districts Show Similar Pattern

New analysis from Economist/YouGov suggested Democratic strength extends beyond heavily blue districts. [...] Nationally, registered voters favored Democrats over Republicans by 4 percentage points. More importantly for control of the House, voters in the 65 most competitive congressional districts preferred Democrats 45 percent to 40 percent, YouGov said.
results.title: Donald Trump Gets Worrying Midterm Warning Sign Across 3 New Polls

results.content: Trump’s slide in the polls in recent weeks could signify good news for Democrats ahead of November’s midterm elections. In the newest Economist/YouGov poll, Democrats hold an 8-point lead over the GOP in a generic congressional ballot.
results.title: Trump's approval rating hits yet another record low in latest poll

results.content:
Polling from YouGov/Economist, Fox News and Echelon Insights shows Trump's standing among independent voters has deteriorated on job approval, the economy, immigration and broader measures of national sentiment heading into the midterms.

At the same time, Democratic candidates have opened a substantial lead among independents on the generic congressional ballot, raising questions about whether dissatisfaction with the president is beginning to translate into broader electoral risk.
